speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; to help me understand your condition, please tell me, at what specific times or activities do these breathing difficulties occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: That combination of stridor worsening with neck flexion (the "sniffing" test) and post-feeding vomiting is highly concerning for a laryngeal web or subglottic stenosis. Have you noticed if the episodes are triggered specifically by milk aspiration during feeds or by upper respiratory infections?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). The classic triad of stridor worsening with neck flexion, crying, and feeding, along with post-prandial vomiting, is pathognomonic for this condition. Please confirm the infant's growth percentiles and whether there are any signs of failure to thrive.
